newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH NPF GIVES CZK 66 BLN TO HELP BANKS 1992-96.
newsitem.headline: CZECH NPF GIVES CZK 66 BLN TO HELP BANKS 1992-96.

text.p: The Czech state privatisation
agency, the National Property Fund (NFP), paid a total of 65.6
billion crowns to support banks from 1992 to 1996, the NPF said
on Friday.
The NPF earned revenue totalling 150.4 billion crowns
during the period through several methods of privatising
thousands of Czech companies of various sizes.
NPF chairman Roman Ceska told a news conference on Friday
that total expenditures by the fund during the period were
144.215 billion crowns.
"A majority of the expenditures went in this or that form
for the support of the banking sector," he said.
"The total (for banks' use) was about 65.5 billion plus 7.2
billion of expenditures connected to bond issues," he added.
More than a dozen small and medium sized Czech banks have
struggled with bad debts and low liquidity after the sector was
liberalised soon after the fall of communism in 1989.
The NPF money was used to help cover non-performing debts
of banks, for direct funds to banks, for state subsidies to
banks, and to help the central bank manage liquidity on the
money market through bond issues.
The NPF did not disclose details on which individual
commercial banks received the help.
While some of the money during the four year period was
used to help the Czech government balance its state budget,
data from the NPF showed that none of the remaining surplus was
intended to help balance the state budget in 1997.
The data showed that no NPF funds were applied to the state
budget in 1996.
Ceska said the still outstanding surplus in the NPF from
privatisation of about six billion crowns would be used in
accounts for various state support programmes.
The money is still to be distributed as follows:
* Three billion crowns are intended to be given to Komercni
Banka for loans that should help exports.
* Another 1.4 billion crowns will act as reserves against
any potential disaster in the operation of the Ingolstadt crude
oil pipeline which connects Czech refineries with the
Transalpine pipeline in Germany.
* About 960 million crowns will be in the form of deposits
at Komercni to help provide a debt restructuring package for
the troubled Czech aircraft maker Aero Vodochody a.s..
* And 224 million crowns would go toward a fund to help
finance Czech non-profit organisations.
In 1997 Ceska said the balance sheet of NPF should be
balanced, as the number of privatisations has significantly
dropped since the massive waves of selloffs from 1992-1995.
